parole.significato: A food of native peoples in western Alaska, consisting of whipped fat mixed with berries and sometimes fish and sugar.
An Alaska Native (traditionally Yup'ik) garment worn on the upper body as an overshirt on top of a parka (“long jacket…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Yup'ik qaspeq, from qai- (“surface; top”) + -peq (postbase denoting something at a certain place).

parole.significato: A soft knee-high boot of sealskin or reindeer skin, originally worn by Inuit and Yupik.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Yup'ik maklak (“bearded seal”), referring to sealskin used to make boots, originally derived from Proto-Eskimo *makla (“bearded seal, spotted seal”).

parole.significato: Catastrophic land collapse caused by the melting of permafrost, coastal flooding and erosion.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Yup'ik uste- (“erode, cave in”). First attested in 2018.

parole.significato: A member of an Eskimo people of western and southwestern Alaska.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Yup'ik Yup'ik (“real person”), from Proto-Eskimo *iŋuɣpiɣ, from *iŋuɣ (“human, person”).
